entry.note: Credit builder. Up to 2 limit increases a year. £0 annual fee.

ladder.reason: You only have one active account. Another card adds limit, which lowers your utilisation, and builds history.

reasons.title: High credit utilisation
reasons.evidence: You're using 79% of your £1,200 card limits. Lenders read that as stretched.

reasons.title: A recent late payment
reasons.evidence: Your Barclaycard payment was late 3 months before you applied.

reasons.title: Only one credit account
reasons.evidence: You have one card, so lenders have little to compare. A second account, used well, helps.

reasons.title: Several applications close together
reasons.evidence: 3 hard searches in the 3 months around your application, including this one.

fix.title: Get your cards under 30% (£348 or less)
fix.how: Pay £175 extra this month, then £215 a month. Your plan shows the date you cross 30%.

reapply.how: Run Capital One QuickCheck first. It's a soft search, so it won't show to other lenders. Only apply if it says yes.

rights: If a lender turns you down because of credit agency data, it must tell you so and name the agency it used (Consumer Credit Act, s157). Your letter names Experian.
You can see your report from Experian for free (your statutory report).
If something is wrong, dispute it with the agency. It's free and they have up to 28 days.
If something is right but has a reason behind it, add a notice of correction (up to 200 words) so lenders see your side.
